    To StartThat's-a-lot-of-Littles cheese puffsStuart meets the whole Little family. Warm gruyere choux puffs, straight from the oven.How to make it125ml water125ml milk100g butter150g plain flour4 eggs120g gruyere, finely grated1/2 tsp Dijon mustardBring the water, milk, butter and a pinch of salt to the boil, tip in the flour and beat until it leaves the sides of the pan.Cool for 5 minutes, then beat in the eggs one at a time until glossy.Beat in the mustard and most of the cheese, then pipe or spoon small balls onto lined trays and top with the rest of the cheese.Bake at 200°C until puffed, golden and crisp.Cereal box cornflake chicken tendersAnton mocks George's boat. Cornflake-crumbed chicken, honey mustard dip.How to make it600g chicken tenderloins75g plain flour2 eggs120g cornflakes, lightly crushed1 tsp sweet paprika3 tbsp olive oil3 tbsp whole-egg mayonnaise2 tbsp honey1 tbsp Dijon mustardSeason the flour, beat the eggs and mix the cornflakes with the paprika.Dip each tender in flour, egg, then cornflakes, and lay on a lined tray.Drizzle with oil and bake at 220°C, turning once, until golden and cooked through.Stir the mayonnaise, honey and mustard together and serve as a dip.A wedge of cheddar for the smallest guestCut it small.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsEleanor's Cajun meatloaf with mash and peasFrederick says the meatloaf is delicious. Cajun-spiced meatloaf, buttery mash, peas.How to make it800g beef mince1 brown onion, finely diced1 red capsicum, finely diced2 tsp Cajun seasoning60g fresh breadcrumbs1 egg125ml milk, plus a splash for the mash125ml tomato sauce2 tbsp brown sugar1kg floury potatoes60g butter2 cups frozen peasMix the mince, onion, capsicum, Cajun seasoning, breadcrumbs, egg, milk and salt with your hands.Shape into a loaf on a lined tray and brush with the tomato sauce mixed with the sugar.Bake at 180°C for 1 hour, then rest for 10 minutes.Meanwhile boil the potatoes and mash with the butter and a splash of milk.Cook the peas, slice the meatloaf and serve with the mash.Snowbell's not-on-the-menu fish pieWe do not eat family members. Creamy fish pie under a mash lid.How to make it600g firm white fish fillets, in chunks200g raw prawns, peeled600ml milk50g butter, plus 40g for the mash3 tbsp plain flour1 cup frozen peas2 tbsp parsley, chopped1kg floury potatoes60g cheddar, gratedBoil the potatoes and mash with the 40g butter and a splash of the milk.Melt the 50g butter, stir in the flour, then whisk in the rest of the milk and simmer until thick.Stir in the fish, prawns, peas and parsley, season and tip into a baking dish.Spread the mash over, scatter with cheese and bake at 200°C until golden and bubbling.Something SweetTen inches tall chocolate layer cakeStuart feels 10 inches tall. Two dark chocolate layers, fudgy frosting.How to make it225g plain flour300g caster sugar60g cocoa powder, plus 30g for the frosting1 1/2 tsp bicarb soda2 eggs250ml buttermilk125ml vegetable oil125ml hot water150g soft butter250g icing sugarWhisk the flour, sugar, 60g cocoa, bicarb and a pinch of salt, then whisk in the eggs, buttermilk, oil and hot water.Divide between two lined 20cm tins and bake at 175°C until a skewer comes out clean.Cool completely.Beat the butter with the icing sugar and 30g cocoa until fluffy, then sandwich and cover the cake.To DrinkBoat race raspberry lemonadeStuart wins George's boat race. Fresh lemons, crushed raspberries, soda.How to make it150g frozen raspberries100g caster sugar100ml water4 lemons, juiced750ml soda water, chilled2 cups ice cubesSimmer the raspberries, sugar and water for 5 minutes, then sieve and cool.Stir in the lemon juice, pour over ice and top with soda.Cold chocolate milkSnowbell is not getting any.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
